the investigation of the relative effectiveness of score normalisation techniques for text-dependent speaker recognition, with a view to improving the verification accuracy of the speaker recognition system.
the investigation of the effectiveness of different score normalisation methods and the analysis of the results of such an investigation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the conditions of this study, the best verification accuracy can be achieved using a form of cohort normalisation.
, for the considered conditions, the use of the best form of the cohort method for score normalisation results in the best verification performance.
the best results were obtained by using a form of cohort normalisation, with the use of a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) to represent the cohort.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cohort normalisation is the best method to normalise the verification scores for the speaker verification task, when the speaker models are based on isolated digits.
the cohort normalisation approach is the best performing normalisation technique in the considered experiments.
the best results are achieved using the proposed form of the cohort-normalisation method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of score normalisation method can have a significant impact on the performance of a speaker verification system.
the choice of score normalisation method is an important factor in the overall performance of a verification system.

the choice of normalisation technique is an important factor in the performance of the verification system, and that a careful analysis of the results of a normalisation technique is necessary to determine whether the technique is suitable for a given application.
